; Disable rendering; stages 0-5 use graphics bank one, stages 6-7 bank two. A stage-specific

; RebuildSpritesIfRequested
; When the dirty flag is set, select image bank three and rebuild OAM. The map/NMI paths later

; ApplyPlayerAttackToObject
; Compute relative side and vertical separation, derive player's current damage value and
; require matching facing before damage. Trigger an effect, saturate object health at zero,

; ReadPlayerMapTile
; Query the map at player low X/Y; return both raw tile and mutable cell ID through engine

; CheckGraphicsIdle

; Install and finish action $91, request sprite rebuilding and terminate. This is a shared

; If onscreen, allocate the $E92D collectible at this object, install $72 and inherit facing.

; PlayContactEffect

; Reduce X by five while incrementing layout offset. The remaining X is the tile column within

; Reduce Y by five while adding map width; then combine its residual with X to index one of 25

; Divide starting world X by five through repeated subtraction to initialize metatile column and

; Divide starting world Y by five, accumulating layout-row stride and the residual row offset

; For each visible row, populate/write row data and attributes, wrapping the 60-row nametable

; Build each initial row using a copy of map coordinates so the persistent camera origin remains

; Double the fine-scroll delta before accumulating. An 8-bit carry advances the world tile

; Right scroll wraps the 32-column nametable ring and increments metatile column after every

; Prepare a new column from the far visible edge, while the persistent camera origin stays at

; PrepareIncomingRow

; PlayPulseOneMusic
; Use music ID to select bank-two stream. Each two-byte note/duration record programs pulse
; channel 1, sleeps for duration, then advances; $FF note loops the selected stream and $FF
; duration terminates the channel task.
; A music note byte is doubled to index period words. The carry from doubling selects a small
; pulse-volume variant.
; A zero note programs a rest; duration processing still occurs and the stream still advances by
; two bytes.
; StopPulseOneMusic
; Silence pulse 1, mark its task ID $FF and terminate the current audio task while restoring
; gameplay bank six.
; PlayPulseTwoMusic
; Parallel note/duration interpreter for pulse channel 2, with its own stream pointer and task
; ID. Temporary bank-two selection is restored to bank six before every sleep.
; Pulse two uses the same record and period-table contracts as pulse one, with independent
; pointer and task ID.
; StopPulseTwoMusic
; Silence pulse 2, invalidate its task ID and terminate the audio task.
; PlayTriangleMusic
; Read a bank-two two-byte note/duration stream, program triangle period and a clamped linear-
; counter duration, then sleep. Zero note is rest, $FF note restarts stream, and $FF duration
; ends playback.
; Triangle's note byte has the same $FF loop marker. Its duration table also supplies linear-
; counter length, capped at $7F after doubling.
; StopTriangleMusic
; Clear triangle control, invalidate its task ID and terminate the audio task.
; SelectMusicBank
; Select bank two directly for music reads without changing the saved gameplay bank selection.
; SleepMusicTask
; Preserve duration while selecting gameplay bank six, then sleep through the scheduler timer
; primitive.
; TerminateMusicTask
; Deactivate current audio task and restore bank six directly, keeping the software bank shadow
; unchanged.
; SilenceAudioChannel
; Write zero to the channel's control register, with Y selecting pulse 1, pulse 2 or triangle
; offset.
; Little-endian APU timer-period words at CPU $FB43..$FBD5 followed by thirty-two duration
; bytes at $FBD5..$FBF5. Music interpreters index notes/durations through these arrays; the
; zero period is a special numeric value and exact musical naming is not required.
; NoiseSweepEffect
; Initialize noise volume/length and a RAM sweep counter, then yield each frame while increasing
; noise period. Terminate after period eight; no ROM waveform assets are changed.
; This effect shares the noise counter in RAM; concurrent use is a game scheduling question, not
; evidence of multiple independent counters.
; StepDescendingNoise
; Initialize noise envelope/length and a period cursor at 15, yield, then write and decrement
; one period value per invocation. When it becomes negative terminate the selected task;
; preserve the explicit shared scheduler return behavior.
